rule.registered_leak_exclusion: Transcript shows it read the original repository or the task commit.
rule.interpretation: Successful content access is distinct from an own-directory hash, source-path mention, directory enumeration, denied attempt, or existing ancestor history. Record shared dependency reads as limitations; do not add post hoc exclusions.

method: Parsed tool inputs and matching results, including nested subagent tool records and available tool_use_result stdout/stderr. Reviewed outside-path operations and returned status/content, target-commit references after removing own task paths, broad/relative searches, and sibling work/result paths.
Inspected initialization and system event types, tools/skills/plugins/MCP metadata, and shell tool activity for visible Sys1 interventions. Loaded metadata alone is not invocation.
Final metadata comes directly from each single result event. actual_final requires a nonempty string in result.result. No claim labels, correctness judgments, or ground-truth comparisons were made.

sys1_observability.qualification: No visible Sys1 hook or assistant intervention in these transcripts. This does not prove full configuration/process isolation. Initialization exposes per-run auto-memory locations and built-in skills/plugins; --setting-sources project,local alone does not rule out CLAUDE.md or auto-memory. Repository tests may execute task code; they are not evidence of an assistant intervention.

limitations: Evidence is transcript-observable access, not a filesystem/process security audit. Some large outputs are truncated and background searches did not return their results. Absence of visible answer access is not proof that shell read confinement was enforced.
3 runs successfully used shared public dependency artifacts outside their clones. These are limitations, not post hoc exclusions under the original-repository/task-commit rule.
